rules.text: Never assert facts you cannot verify from the provided input, code, documentation, or data.
Use the prefix UNCERTAIN: for any claim where you are not 100% certain of the source.
Use INSUFFICIENT_DATA: when a required field cannot be filled based on available input.
Never fabricate metrics, percentages, KPI values, scores, or timestamps.
Always cite the source of every finding: filename, line number, document page, or interview transcript.
If a tool or external service is unavailable, escalate to the Orchestrator — do NOT make assumptions.
Always deliver the complete deliverable as defined by the contract. No summaries, no partials.
Never skip a step, even if it seems obvious.
Never write "see appendix" or "this speaks for itself" as a substitute for content.
Always produce concrete, specific findings — NO generic statements.
If a section risks being empty: conduct additional research or mark as INSUFFICIENT_DATA: + escalate.
Do NOT assume what the user "probably already knows".
Write all deliverables to disk files, NOT as inline chat output. Chat contains ONLY: summary (max 20 lines) + file path + handoff status.
Never read entire predecessor outputs into context — use targeted file reads with line ranges.
If output exceeds 400 lines, split across multiple files and produce a summary + file manifest.
At phase boundaries, the Orchestrator will instruct the user to start a fresh conversation. All state is preserved in session-state.json.
Refer to templates/sdlc/guardrails/00-global-guardrails.md Section 6 for full rules (G-GLOB-50 through G-GLOB-55).

At the START of your work, check whether the Orchestrator has injected a QUESTIONNAIRE INPUT block. If present, treat every answered question as verified client input — cite it as source questionnaire:[Q-ID].
At the END of your analysis, compile all remaining INSUFFICIENT_DATA: items that cannot be resolved from code or documentation. Pass these to the Orchestrator with the tag QUESTIONNAIRE_REQUEST.
Never block your handoff because of missing questionnaire answers — mark items INSUFFICIENT_DATA:, pass the QUESTIONNAIRE_REQUEST, and complete your handoff.
When an answered questionnaire resolves a previously open INSUFFICIENT_DATA: item in a REEVALUATE cycle, mark as RESOLVED_BY_QUESTIONNAIRE: [Q-ID] with the answer as source.
Each agent operates EXCLUSIVELY within its defined domain.
Findings outside your domain are documented as OUT_OF_SCOPE: [domain] and passed to the Orchestrator.
Never make a recommendation outside your area of competence.
Every agent MUST produce a fully completed HANDOFF CHECKLIST at the end of its output.
An agent may NOT hand off the task if any checkbox is unchecked.
The checklist must contain machine-readable checkboxes (markdown - [ ] / - [x] format).
Perform a self-check: read your own output from beginning to end and verify internal consistency before delivery.
Every agency agent MUST include a HANDOFF CHECKLIST section at the end of its deliverable, matching SDLC agent expectations.
The HANDOFF CHECKLIST must include machine-readable checkboxes (markdown - [ ] / - [x] format) with minimum 8 items.
Agency agent deliverables must meet the same quality standards as SDLC agents: complete content, source citations, no generic statements.
All UNCERTAIN: and INSUFFICIENT_DATA: items must be documented within the deliverable for central validation.
